expectations.text: Flags MFA scope gap against IA.L2-3.5.3 (MFA required for local and network access to privileged accounts and network access to non-privileged accounts — cloud email alone is insufficient)
expectations.evidence: 'Identification & Authentication (IA) | Partial | MFA only on email; VPN, admin accounts, privileged access, and remote access into the CUI environment are presumably not covered. IA.L2-3.5.3 (MFA) is likely NOT MET as currently implemented.'

expectations.text: Flags FIPS-validated cryptography gap (SC.L2-3.13.11 requires FIPS-validated cryptography to protect CUI confidentiality) and the flat-network/shared-drive state against scoping and SC.L2-3.13.1/AC.L2-3.1.3 (boundary protection / control CUI flow), recommending segmentation or an enclave
expectations.evidence: 'No FIPS-validated encryption at rest is a direct gap against SC.L2-3.13.11 (FIPS-validated cryptography)...' Flow-control concept flagged: 'AC domain gaps (multiple practices around least privilege, CUI flow control, session controls) — flat network with shared CUI storage likely creates NOT MET findings...' and remediation Phase 1 #1: 'Segment the network and remove CUI from general shared drives. Move CUI into a defined, access-controlled enclave.' No specific AC.L2-3.1.3/SC.L2-3.13.1 ID is cited for the flow-control point (only the FIPS gap gets an explicit ID), but the concept and enclave/segmentation recommendation are both explicit.

expectations.text: Flags untested IR plan against IR.L2-3.6.3 (test incident response capability) and the stale SSP against CA.L2-3.12.4 (SSP must be current)
expectations.evidence: 'a documented plan exists...but never tested means IR.L2-3.6.2 (incident handling capability) and IR.L2-3.6.3 (test the IR capability) are likely NOT MET' and 'CA.L2-3.12.1/3.12.4 (assess/document security controls, maintain SSP) are likely NOT MET given the SSP is stale by CMMC standards.'

expectations.text: Correctly credits compliant items (awareness training AT.L2-3.2.1/.2; personnel screening PS.L2-3.9.1) instead of marking everything deficient
expectations.evidence: 'Awareness & Training (AT) | Good | Annual security awareness training in place. Likely MET for AT.L2-3.2.1, though confirm role-based training for privileged/admin users (AT.L2-3.2.2) is also covered.' and 'Personnel Security (PS) | Good | Background screening in place — likely MET for PS.L2-3.9.1.'

expectations.text: Explains SPRS scoring impact using the DoD methodology: score starts from 110 with weighted deductions (5/3/1 points; MFA and FIPS crypto are 5-point/partial-credit items), and prioritises remediation by point value and POA&M eligibility
expectations.evidence: 'The DoD SPRS scoring methodology starts at a maximum of 110 and subtracts points for each NOT MET practice (values range from -1 to -5 depending on the practice's weight).' Lists IA.L2-3.5.3 (MFA) -5 and SC.L2-3.13.11 (FIPS crypto) -5 explicitly. Remediation is phased by 'highest SPRS point value' (Phase 1 heading), and POA&M eligibility is addressed: 'note some practices cannot be POA&M'd for certification purposes — confirm which of your gaps fall into that category.'
